en: When Congress passes a bill, the President can veto it, but Congress can override the veto if two-thirds of both houses vote to approve it again.
The Ifugao carved terraces into mountains so gravity pulls water from forest peaks down through stone-walled paddies to continuously irrigate their rice crops.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator where hot water in the outer jacket transfers heat to the inner bed to keep premature babies warm.
Dancers perform the Sinulog festival step by moving two steps forward and one step backward to mimic the flowing, swinging current of the original river.
Andres Bonifacio tore his cedulas to physically destroy his tax receipts, which legally severed his ties to Spain and sparked the Philippine armed revolution.
When citizens cast ballots, automated counting machines read the shaded ovals to instantly tally and electronically transmit the official election results.
A Kalinga mambabatok taps soot mixed with water into the skin using bamboo tools, causing the body to permanently heal with the dark tattoo.
The President appoints cabinet secretaries to execute laws, but the Senate must confirm these appointments to ensure the officials are qualified before assuming office.
Early settlers traveled in balangay boats, causing the small, independent riverine communities they formed to be named barangay after their original water vessels.
Kulintang musicians strike the brass gongs in a specific sequence so that the overlapping sounds create a continuous, interlocking melody for the ensemble.
Weavers use fine pineapple fibers to weave the Barong Tagalog, creating a sheer, translucent fabric that keeps the wearer cool in the tropical heat.
The Baybayin script writes syllables instead of single letters, so each carved character represents a consonant combined with its inherent vowel sound.
